fact: ESCCOM, through the Universal Access Service Fund, co-funded and launched the Macetjeni iHub in rural Lubombo Region on 6 August 2026 with SEDCO and UNDP, giving young people, women and others internet access and digital skills training; it follows a first iHub at Piggs Peak.

ICT Principal Secretary Prince Mashishimba Andreas Dlamini said on 9 October 2026 that government plans to use Eswatini Post offices as community digital centres to bring public services to rural and underserved communities.

The Ministry of ICT is implementing the E1.2 billion (US$65 million) Eswatini Digital Project, with E648 million for Affordable Broadband including fibre expansion and last mile connectivity, and says it will extend connectivity to underserved rural areas.

The Government of Eswatini commissioned a Starlink Satellite Gateway on 28 April 2026, which TechAfrica News says is expected to bring faster internet to remote and underserved areas that mobile towers and fibre have not reached.
